scenario: AITA for not believing my coworker about “chronic pain”? | I have a coworker in his mid 30s who claims to suffer from chronic pain. Frankly, I think it’s a load of crap. Some days he’s limping around the office or even calls in sick claiming he’s in too bad of pain to come into the office. He’ll be wincing and just sitting in his chair. He claims it’s from a botched surgery. Somehow he’s been granted FMLA. There are plenty of other days though when he’s walking around just fine, even talking walks in the park across from our office or standing around at a coworker’s desk laughing while they talk. I’ve made comments like “Gee, you look like you’re really hurting!” on those days and he just says “I’m having a good day. They happen.” Recently he started using a cane as a prop, which is when I confronted him. There’s no way it’s legitimate need. I asked him just how bad his surgery was that now he needs a cane, adding that it was taking the act a bit too far. He pulled up his shirt and revealed a dinky little 4” scar near his waist. I said laughed and said “That’s why you’re stumbling around?” He replied “This is the outside. I hope you get to feel what I feel, asshole.” Then he shuffled away with his cane and next thing I know I’m getting talked to by our boss about how I’m treating Mr. Pain and that it’s inappropriate. When I told my boss I knew he was faking, he told me “his doctors know more than you” and that if I ever voiced doubt about the coworker in the office again, I’d be looking for a new job.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out what to do about this situation with my coworker. He's in his mid-30s and claims to have chronic pain. I'm not sure if I believe him because sometimes he seems fine, walking around the office, talking to other coworkers, even going for walks in the park. But other days, he's limping around or calling in sick, saying he's in too much pain to come into the office. He's been granted FMLA, which I think is Family and Medical Leave Act, so he's supposed to be getting medical treatment or something. Then, recently, he started using a cane, and that's when I confronted him. I told him that there's no way it's a legitimate need, and I asked him how bad his surgery was that now he needs a cane. I said it was taking the act too far. He pulled up his shirt and showed me a tiny little 4-inch scar near his waist. I laughed and said, "That's why you're stumbling around?" He replied, "This is the outside. I hope you get to feel what I feel, asshole," and shuffled away with his cane. Then, I got talked to by my boss about how I'm treating Mr. Pain and that it's inappropriate. When I told my boss I knew he was faking, my boss said his doctors know more than me and that if I ever voice doubt about the coworker again, I'd be looking for a new job. So, I'm feeling really stuck. I don't want to lose my job, but I also don't think my coworker is being honest about his condition. How do I handle this? Is there a way to address my concerns without getting into trouble? Maybe I should talk to HR or someone else about this, but I'm not sure. I don't want to make things worse, but I also don't want to keep working in an environment where I feel like someone is taking advantage of the system. I guess I need to figure out what my options are. Can I document the times when he seems fine versus when he's claiming to be in pain? Maybe that could help if there's any investigation. But I'm not sure if that's the right approach. I also wonder if there's a way to support him without believing his claims. Maybe I should just keep my opinions to myself and focus on my work. This is really confusing. I don't want to be the bad guy, but I also don't want to be silent if I think something's wrong. I need to find a balance between standing up for what I believe and maintaining a good relationship with my employer and coworkers.
